title: Embeddings route canary amplification — incident review and corrective actions
creator: Ava Martinez
description: During a canary rollout of a new embeddings model variant (embed-v2.1-canary), we observed an amplification in cross-region fanout that caused tiered circuit breakers to saturate and led to a sustained SLO slip for the embeddings route (p95 generation latency and availability). This ticket documents the incident review, immediate mitigations, root cause analysis, and tracked corrective actions to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2025-09-30T02:14Z - Canary traffic ramp started (5% global) via rollout controller
2025-09-30T02:17Z - First elevated p95 on embeddings-prod-us-east; alert EMB-P95-THRESHOLD fired
2025-09-30T02:19Z - Circuit-breaker metrics showing per-region saturation; control-plane routing attempted failover to secondary regions
2025-09-30T02:22Z - Autoscaler started warm-up but observed asymmetric warmup across regions due to placement constraints
2025-09-30T02:28Z - Fallback traffic to embed-v2.0 caused KV-cache coldstarts on secondaries and priority-queue inversion for latency-sensitive requests
2025-09-30T02:40Z - On-call initiated manual canary rollback; traffic restored to baseline by 2025-09-30T02:46Z
2025-09-30T03:10Z - Incident declared over; SLOs recovered to expected ranges by 03:25Z
impact: External: ~4% of production embeddings requests experienced p95 latency > 1.5s for a 30-minute window; availability dropped below 99.5% for that window. Internal: cross-region egress and GPU utilization spiked, billing anomaly detected. Customers using high-frequency embedding refresh saw degraded syncs.
root_causes: Canary rollout caused a small request-weight shift to a model variant with higher per-request initialization CPU pressure, exposing cold KV-cache behavior on secondary regions.
Smart routing fallback logic routed by model-compatibility instead of latency during control-plane contention, unintentionally amplifying fanout to under-warmed regions.
Tiered circuit-breaker hysteresis settings were too aggressive for brief bursts, causing synchronized trip across regions rather than gradual shedding.
Autoscaler warmup and placement constraints (bin-packing policy) delayed capacity availability in secondary regions, lengthening the period of degraded performance.
detection: Primary detection by Synthetic SLO monitors and the EMB-P95-THRESHOLD alert. Engineers correlated alert spikes with canary rollout events via the rollout-controller audit log and route decision traces in the tracing dashboard.
mitigation: Immediate: halted canary rollout and rolled back to embed-v2.0 to stop additional amplification (actioned at 02:40Z).
Throttled cross-region fallback for embeddings route to a maximum of 10% during the incident window to avoid cascade to cold regions.
Temporarily increased circuit-breaker recovery window to limit oscillation while autoscalers completed warmup.
action_items: (Rohit) Stabilize canary rollout: implement incremental ramp with per-region warmup checks and a global safety gate that verifies KV-cache hit-rate >= 80% before next percent step — due 2025-10-15
(Maya Chen) Change routing policy to prefer route latency when control-plane contention is detected; add a compatibility fallback only when latency targets are met — due 2025-10-10
(Diego Alvarez) Tune tiered circuit-breaker hysteresis: introduce randomized recovery jitter and per-region staggered reset to avoid synchronized trips — due 2025-10-12
(SRE team) Add a short-lived pre-warm phase in autoscaler for canaries to allocate minimal KV-cache priming tokens and reduce coldstarts for model init — due 2025-10-08

(Observability) Create an embeddings canary dashboard showing per-region kv-cache hit-rate, model-init CPU, and per-queue latency, and wire a composite alert for correlated degradation — owner: Priya, due 2025-10-07
(Billing) Investigate egress spike and produce customer-facing summary if external costs > $5k unusual spend — owner: Erin, due 2025-10-14
follow_ups: Run a synthetic canary exercise with embed-v2.1 in a staging multi-region footprint that replicates placement constraints (2025-10-06).
Create a runbook entry: 'embeddings-canary-fanout' describing safe rollback criteria, throttling knobs, and quick KV-cache priming steps (owner: SRE, due 2025-10-09).
Evaluate feasibility of per-tenant adaptive throttling for high-frequency embedding customers to avoid global amplification (product review Q4).
notes: Control-plane routing logic had an undocumented edge case where compatibility_score override was favored during transient capacity pressure; this will be surfaced in design review.
We observed a small subset of tenants with heavy synchronous refresh patterns contributed disproportionally to load; consider tenant-level backpressure policies.

This incident shows interaction class: canary deployment x placement constraint x circuit hysteresis; single-point mitigations are insufficient without coordination across rollout, routing, and autoscaling layers.
